key_insight: GPU-optimized fast diagonalization and matrix-free preconditioners accelerate high-order finite-element elliptic solves by reducing both iteration counts and per-iteration costs.
engineering_relevance: These methods can shorten large-scale elliptic solves in engineering simulations, with solver choice guided by mesh structure and coefficient variation.
method: Distributed direct fast diagonalization for tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate.
Hybrid Schwarz with exact local fast-diagonalization solves and p-multigrid with fused hanging-node constraint handling.
Selective FP32 work within FP64 conjugate gradients, adaptive coarse-level distribution, and multiple-right-hand-side support across CUDA, HIP, and SYCL.
evidence_signal: Evaluations across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs report 100–1,000× faster direct solves than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes and 11 HS-FD iterations on generalized Poisson octree problems across 8–1,024 MI250X compute dies.
watch_item: The direct solver requires tensor-product structure and restricted coefficient variation; selective FP32 use also depends on cell shapes and coefficients.
paper_title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
